bull.t: Strong revenue acceleration and backlog growth
bull.b: Rapid revenue growth, expanding backlog, and substantial booked orders provide evidence of increasing customer adoption and near-term demand visibility. If management converts the pipeline as planned, higher volume could support operating leverage and strengthen TOMI’s position in regulated disinfection markets.

bull.t: Recurring consumables support the business model
bull.b: Consumable revenue tied to installed SteraMist systems can create repeat purchasing beyond the initial equipment sale. This recurring component may improve customer lifetime value, increase revenue visibility, and provide a durable growth engine as the installed base expands.

New regulatory approvals, patent applications, and customer deployments broaden the addressable use cases for TOMI’s technology. Progress across food safety, healthcare, life sciences, and international markets can reinforce differentiation and create multiple avenues for longer-term commercial adoption.

bear.t: Persistent losses and negative cash generation
bear.b: TOMI has not yet demonstrated sustainable profitability or internally funded growth. Persistent operating and free-cash-flow deficits consume financial resources, increase reliance on outside capital, and could limit the company’s ability to invest consistently in sales, regulatory work, and expansion.

High leverage relative to equity leaves TOMI with less capacity to absorb execution setbacks or fund growth without additional financing. Combined with substantial losses, the elevated debt burden may increase refinancing pressure and constrain management’s strategic and operating choices.

bear.t: Funding and regulatory milestones remain uncertain
bear.b: TOMI’s growth plans depend partly on capital access and regulatory milestones that are not fully assured. Delays in financing or approvals could postpone commercialization, raise execution costs, and prevent the company from converting its pipeline into durable revenue and cash generation.
